name: Marcus Garvey
role: Jamaican-born founder and President-General of the Universal Negro Improvement Association (1914-1940)
summary: Garvey was a Black nationalist and Pan-Africanist who built the UNIA around racial pride, economic self-reliance and the return of the Black diaspora to a free, united Africa. He favoured each race having its own homeland, opposed racial mixing and integration, defended armed struggle for African liberation, rejected Communism while accepting a limited capitalism, and proposed a strong elected executive held to account by the threat of death.

booksNotUsed.reason: Project Gutenberg's catalog has no work by Marcus Garvey (searched by name; the only 'Garvey' hit is an unrelated 1963 volume by James Emmett Garvey).

unions-good.rationale: He told Negro workers to avoid affiliating with white trade unions and to keep their wage scale below the white union rate, yet his 1937 course credits the UNIA with teaching Negroes to run their own labor organisations.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In his proposal on capitalism and the state he caps any corporation's holdings at five million and lets the state conscript the wealth of corporations whose foreign ventures cause wars.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Declaration he signed demands 'free speech universally for all men' and protests inflammatory press only as an abuse, asking for no legal restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: He proposed that an elected president hold absolute authority, appointing all cabinet ministers, governors, administrators and judges, answerable with his life for abuse.

state-harmful.rationale: He builds his programme on founding a government and nation for Negroes ('a government second to none') and a strong state in Africa.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He says the Negro has a claim on white sympathy and asks white America to help Negroes return to Africa, while insisting Negroes must liberate themselves.

revolution-justified.rationale: He tells followers that any race wanting freedom must first think in terms of blood, holds up Washington, the French and Lenin as models, and says armed struggle for Africa is justified.

democracy-best.rationale: He ties the Negro's goal to 'true democracy' and democratic institutions in Africa, and tells his followers democracy is the safest government for those who wish to rise in business.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Declaration he signed calls the attempt to free oneself by war justifiable, and he says liberation must contain force; he separately rejects rioting by citizens within their own countries.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He argues every race should be apportioned its own habitat (Europe for Europeans, Asia for Asiatics, Africa for Africans) to avoid race war.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: He teaches that God made nature for man's use and that man should harness, subdue and use the elements.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He insists God created all races equal and that Negro backwardness comes from lack of self-knowledge and organisation, pointing to the ancient greatness of Egypt and Ethiopia.

national-rebirth.rationale: His Easter 1922 sermon calls for a resurrection of the Negro race from its lethargy so it can return to the glory Ethiopia once held.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He cites 'the great cry of Palestine for the Jews' as one of the political readjustments that follow natural lines, alongside Ireland for the Irish and Africa for the Africans.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: He declares all Negroes worldwide free citizens of Africa, demands Africa 'for the Africans at home and abroad', and protests laws that hinder Negro immigration.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Declaration of Rights he presided over and signed states 'We believe in the self-determination of all peoples', and he named Palestine, Ireland, India and Africa as peoples each needing a home.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration he signed protests segregated districts and separate public conveyances, but he separately seeks territorial separation of the races by emigration rather than segregation by law.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He writes that rulers chosen by the masses forget their obligation and arrogate the good of the nation to themselves, and that graft and greed have caused government to fail.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The UNIA, in his name, declares itself against miscegenation and race suicide, and he calls on both races to oppose it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration he signed demands even-handed justice before all courts, and he accords all men the rights he claims.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He states that government is only an expression of the will of the people, and tells followers who cannot vote to win the vote or be 'governed without your consent'.

separated-powers.rationale: His proposed government gives the elected president absolute power to appoint all officials and judges, with no separate body checking him other than the penalty for betraying the trust.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He argues that where races share a country the stronger majority will not yield power, producing clashes, so each race needs its own country.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Declaration he signed states belief in the freedom of the press and protests suppression of newspapers.

death-penalty.rationale: He urges that corrupt officials and judges be put to death or stoned after public disgrace, so he accepts execution by the state for the gravest betrayals.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He says a race can be saved only through a solid industrial foundation together with political independence, and that a race dependent on another economically sooner or later dies.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He proposes that a president who deceives, grafts or favours interests be publicly disgraced and put to death, and that officials be held to the same strict account.

leader-cult.rationale: He proposes public honour, a place in the Hall of Fame and public funerals for presidents who serve faithfully.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The UNIA's declared aim is to unite all Negroes in a single great nation in Africa, and he says all Africa will stand together.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: He says the ballot and industrial progress will not save Negroes in white countries and that their future outside Africa 'spells ruin and disaster'.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He rejects white rule in Africa and says returning Negroes must not exercise over-lordship over natives, though the UNIA's objects include helping to civilize backward tribes.

elective-rulers.rationale: His plan for reformed government assumes a president chosen by election ('when we elect a President'), and he supports Negroes electing their own representatives.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Declaration he signed holds there is no obligation to obey a tax levy by a body excluding the Negro, though his 1937 lessons urge changing laws by vote, not riot.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He writes that capitalism is necessary to the progress of the world and that those who wantonly fight it are enemies of human advancement, while adding that it needs limits.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He calls capitalism necessary to the world's progress, with limits, and rejects Communism as a failed system the Negro should shun, so he holds that at least one of them is sound.

historical-land-claim.rationale: He claims Africa as the Negro's by inherent right and treats European rule as alien intrusion, while citing the Jewish claim to Palestine as comparable.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He condemns European powers for taking African produce and wealth to feed and rehabilitate Europe while Africans starve, and demands they leave Africa.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He says he has no faith in disarmament and that attempts to disarm while half the world oppresses the other half are a farce.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He argues that monopoly in a few hands leaves the masses in want and brings governments down, and proposes caps on individual and corporate capital for that reason.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Declaration he signed accepts battle for national self-defense, and he defends keeping a gun at home against the robber.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He honours the heroes and martyrs of freedom, and says Negroes owe their forebears' sacrifice a free and redeemed Africa.

racial-group-interests.rationale: His central doctrine is that each race must organise to protect its own interests, since 'no race trusts the other' and unorganised groups are at the mercy of the organised.

racial-pride.rationale: He tells Negroes to be as proud of their race as their fathers were, and the UNIA 'believes that the Negro race is as good as any other, and therefore should be as proud of itself'.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Declaration he signed grounds rights on the claim that all men are created equal and entitled to life, liberty and happiness.

race-social-construct.rationale: He treats races as natural, calls for a pure black race, and says the Ethiopian cannot change his skin.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: He wants a Negro government strong enough to protect members of the race scattered worldwide, as great governments protect their citizens from lynching.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Declaration he signed says laws singling out Negroes or taking African land are unjust and immoral and should not be respected.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: He built the UNIA's economic programme on Black-owned enterprise, selling stock in the Black-owned Black Star Steamship Line as part of an agenda of economic independence for the race.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: He repeatedly says Negroes must be ready to die for African freedom ('Liberty or Death') and that he would rather die than not work for it.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He treats alien rule in Africa as an occupation to be ended by force if needed, condemns the machine-gunning of rebels in Kenya and the bombing of Hottentots, and says Negroes must be prepared to die for Africa.

notes: Only Garvey's own texts were used. Searched all themes in the two-volume Philosophy and Opinions and the 1937 Message to the People: economy (capitalism, communism, unions, property caps), government (executive power, democracy, voting), society (race, religion, family, race mixing), world (colonialism, self-determination, war, disarmament, League of Nations), means (force, revolution, constitutional agitation), liberty (press and speech) and ecology and technology (little). Positions were stated in the 1920s and kept in his 1937 course; no sustained change was found. Many statements on economy detail, ecology, technology, gender and religion in public life have no stated position and are null. His racial separatism and his praise of the Klan's honesty are recorded as he stated them.
